note: A sluice row in state=held is STILL LIVE, and resubmitting the same SHA is not free. campaign/the-kerf was held for ordering behind campaign/the-zenith. the-zenith then went CHAMBER RED rc=11 with main unmoved, so I re-checked the mouth and resubmitted the same SHA. Both halves of that were wrong. The held row was released by the operator and is the row that landed (all merge phases rc=0 in 1867s, main 4f303d3b0..cf95817d3). And the resubmit became a duplicate the queue could NOT collapse: coalescing never supersedes a RUNNING request, which is correct in itself, but it leaves a second queued row for a sha already in the chamber -- and sluice-queue.sh claim --sha selects the first QUEUED row, so a drain would have launched a concurrent second merge of the same commit. The operator dropped it by hand. THE RULE: held is an operator state meaning not-now, not a refusal handing the request back. The submitting-to-the-sluice skill line about submit again, a new request not a retry, is about a BOUNCED request whose sha must change. A hold changes nothing about the candidate, so there is nothing to resubmit. If a hold looks stale, post a notice and let the operator release it. LATENT DEFECT WORTH A ROW FOR WHOEVER OWNS THE QUEUE NEXT: claim --sha has no dedup against a RUNNING row at the same sha, so the only thing standing between a stale-looking hold and two concurrent merges of one commit is an operator noticing.
